investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T16:16–16:24Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 128–144 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the agent pod never started, the runner could not collect any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only two nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes able to accept the pod and preemption offering no relief, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never receives a running VM, so it cannot write any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), and the check fails with a full contract gap. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is currently confirmed only at the observability eval layer.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 nodes, meaning the allocatable VM slots are fully consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods. This is the most directly evidenced cause (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: 4 of 6 nodes are structurally ineligible for remote-agent pods due to label or taint constraints. If the two kata-capable nodes are removed, drained, or cordoned, the effective schedulable pool drops to zero even before resource exhaustion.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user-created agents that were not cleaned up may be occupying the finite VM resource slots on the two eligible nodes, preventing new pods from scheduling.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — transient cluster event (node pressure, rolling restart, maintenance): a temporary reduction in node capacity could produce the same scheduler message; however, the failure spans three sequential checks over ~7 minutes (16:16–16:24Z), making a brief transient less likely.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T16:19–16:24Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested kata peer-pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 128–144 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the kata peer-pod node pool; it is an eval-detected signal of a production infrastructure constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence).

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 nodes and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving zero viable placement targets.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and making the cluster highly sensitive to any VM quota pressure on those 2 nodes.

Tertiary — concurrent eval or workload contention: if multiple eval runs or production workloads submitted kata peer-pod requests simultaneously, the small 2-node affinity pool could be transiently exhausted even if nominal capacity is sufficient for steady-state load.

Lower confidence — eval runner token or org resolution failure causing createAgent to be called with bad parameters: ruled less likely because the scheduler error message is explicit and all three sibling checks share the same scheduling failure message, not an auth or org error.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T16:16–16:24Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 128–144 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the agent pod never started, the runner could not collect any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only two nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes able to accept the pod and preemption offering no relief, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never receives a running VM, so it cannot write any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), and the check fails with a full contract gap. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is currently confirmed only at the observability eval layer.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 nodes, meaning the allocatable VM slots are fully consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods. This is the most directly evidenced cause (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: 4 of 6 nodes are structurally ineligible for remote-agent pods due to label or taint constraints. If the two kata-capable nodes are removed, drained, or cordoned, the effective schedulable pool drops to zero even before resource exhaustion.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user-created agents that were not cleaned up may be occupying the finite VM resource slots on the two eligible nodes, preventing new pods from scheduling.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — transient cluster event (node pressure, rolling restart, maintenance): a temporary reduction in node capacity could produce the same scheduler message; however, the failure spans three sequential checks over ~7 minutes (16:16–16:24Z), making a brief transient less likely.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T16:19–16:24Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested kata peer-pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 128–144 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the kata peer-pod node pool; it is an eval-detected signal of a production infrastructure constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was returned by any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned and the eval probe never reached the runtime response stage.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Of 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible by node affinity/selector for remote agent pods, and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM resource quota on those nodes is fully consumed. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 128–150 seconds before the probe timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract gap (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all missing). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes — concurrent remote agent workloads or a prior eval run left VMs allocated and unreleased, leaving no capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift — 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes and amplifying any capacity pressure.

Tertiary: Leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from a previous eval run that did not complete cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 may not have released resources if a prior run was interrupted), holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots occupied.

Lower confidence: Cluster node count or VM resource limit was recently reduced, shrinking available capacity below what concurrent eval probes require — no source or incident evidence supports this directly.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the two affinity-eligible nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable > Requests (i.e., capacity is available), the exhaustion hypothesis is wrong and the scheduler message would need a different explanation.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and returns all required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload briefly consumed capacity) rather than a sustained resource exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector rules were recently changed to exclude more nodes and the 2 remaining nodes have sufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, the root cause would be a misconfigured affinity rule rather than resource exhaustion.
If all 6 nodes show Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (not just 2), the affinity/selector constraint is not the limiting factor and the entire cluster is out of peer-pod VM capacity.
If the eval runner logs show that withCleanup successfully released all resources from prior runs, leaked VMs are not the cause and the exhaustion must come from non-eval workloads.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on affinity-eligible nodes and warns when headroom falls below the number of concurrent remote-agent eval pods needed.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods remain in Pending or Running state after the eval suite completes, catching resource leaks from interrupted withCleanup paths.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 3), alerting before capacity exhaustion becomes inevitable.

Refine the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime evals to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as structured evidence, making future scheduling failures immediately diagnosable without log inspection.
